extracted.intended_audience: General Wikipedia readers and editors (students, researchers, journalists, the interested public)
extracted.subtask_short: encyclopedia article about a think tank
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia encyclopedia article profiling the American Enterprise Institute (AEI): its history, personnel, research programs, political stance, controversies, and bibliographic references. Intended to be a neutral, referenced overview for general readers and researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer secondary or tertiary sources over primary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: This section relies excessively on references to primary sources. Please improve this section by adding secondary or tertiary sources. Find sources: "American Enterprise Institute" – news · newspapers · books · scholar · JSTOR (September 2024) (Learn how and when to remove this message)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the page has been flagged, replace or supplement primary-source citations (e.g., organizational publications, press releases, self-published material) with independent secondary or tertiary coverage (news articles, books, scholarly analysis). The template text explicitly instructs editors to add such sources and provides search hints (news, books, JSTOR, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reliable references / avoid lacking reliable references
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles lacking reliable references from September 2024; All articles lacking reliable references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite reliable, independent, third‑party sources to verify assertions. Avoid relying solely on self-published materials, partisan blogs, or unverified claims. Where warnings/tags appear, add citations from reputable newspapers, academic journals, books, or official records to remove the maintenance tag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use American English spelling and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use American English from April 2026; All Wikipedia articles written in American English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow American English orthography, grammar, and usage throughout the article (e.g., 'organization' not 'organisation', American punctuation conventions). This is a site‑style expectation for consistency with the English Wikipedia variant noted on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use month-day-year (MDY) date format
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format dates in articles using the month-day-year style (e.g., January 1, 2007) consistent with the project's locale guideline noted on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include coordinates on Wikidata
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure geographic coordinates for the subject (headquarters, locations) are present and synchronized with the Wikidata item so they appear in the article's infobox and map tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short description should match Wikidata / be consistent
rubrics_metrics.description: Short description is different from Wikidata
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the article's short description concise and ensure it is consistent with the corresponding Wikidata short description to avoid conflicting metadata between Wikipedia and Wikidata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and mark potentially dated statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles containing potentially dated statements from 2005; All articles containing potentially dated statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag time‑sensitive claims (e.g., financial figures, staff lists, rankings) and update them with current sources or add contextualizing dates. Editors should check and refresh statements that may no longer be accurate and add 'as of' dates where appropriate.
